newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil soars as futures hit five-year highs.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil soars as futures hit five-year highs.

text.p: NWE gas oil strengthened on Monday as benchmark IPE futures hit five-year highs, but traders said the strong outright price levels had dampened activity in the physical market.

The IPE September contract ended the day $11 up at a five-year high of $207.50 a tonne. "There's plenty of talk but a lot of people are reluctant to commmit themselves at these levels and are waiting to see what New York does tomorrow," one trader said. NYMEX was closed on Monday due to the Labor Day holiday.
On the barge market, 4,000 tonnes of heating oil traded at an outright price of $206.50, $1.25 above the screen at the time, for first half September delivery.
On the cargoes, German heating oil was talked at premiums of Sept +$4.50/+$5.0 a tonne, cif Hamburg.
Traders said low German household stocks, a pick-up in French heating oil demand and renewed Brazilian interest in NWE cargoes were keeping premiums strong.
On the low sulphur side, premiums were quoted at Oct IPE +$13/+$15 a tonne.
